However, the NL2 sentence 'This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected' is grammatically ambiguous: the indefinite article 'a' preceding the disjunction could indicate a single detection condition ('a possible [one of three] collision is detected'), in which case Possible_collision_detected faithfully represents that unified condition. The defeater survives because the NL does not explicitly enumerate three separate trigger events or use the UML-precise 'orthogonal' qualifier to disambiguate.

Under the primary typed reading (canonical UML concurrent regions), the model has only 1, establishing the mismatch. None of the three specific collision events appear as triggers on this transition. The three specific events are declared in the model but used only on internal transitions (FCIdle->FCActive, RCIdle->RCActive, PCIdle->PCActive) that are in unreachable states.
issues.reason: The NL2 trigger contract requires the entry transition to be triggered by the three specific collision events. The model uses a different event (Possible_collision_detected) that is semantically broader but not identical to any of the three required events. The three required events are declared in the model but not used as triggers on the entry transition. This is a trigger set mismatch on the exact bound transition.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event Possible_collision_detected could be interpreted as the author's unified representation of 'a possible collision of any type is detected,' semantically encompassing the three specific collision types. The NL says 'a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected' which could be read as a single generalized detection condition rather than three separate triggers.
issues.title: Entry transition to CA uses wrong trigger event

issues.basis: NL3 segment; FCSTM text showing CA's body with Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian, UnspecifiedInitial but no -- separator lines; canonical_source_ir concurrent_regions count=0; inspection_equivalent_facts showing all three composites reachable_from_initial=false; PlantUML source confirming no region separators in the CA block
issues.expected: CA (the active mode of collision avoidance) must be structured with orthogonal (concurrent) regions that permit simultaneous activation of the three collision avoidance controls (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian). In UML, this requires -- separators within CA to create distinct concurrent regions.
issues.observed: CA contains Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian, and UnspecifiedInitial as children in a single implicit region with no -- separators. The canonical_source_ir confirms concurrent_regions count=0. Without orthogonal region structure, entering CA activates only its single initial state (UnspecifiedInitial), not all three collision avoidance sub-composites concurrently. The three composites are unreachable from any execution path.
issues.reason: NL3 explicitly requires orthogonal regions for concurrent activation. The FCSTM model shows CA has no region separators, resulting in a single implicit region where only one initial target is activated. The deterministic reachability facts confirm all three operating composites are unreachable, which is the behavioral consequence of the missing region structure. No frozen predicate directly expresses region_structure, so this remains a predicate-null candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: In some UML tool interpretations, a composite state with multiple child states may implicitly support concurrent execution of those children without explicit -- separators. If the FCSTM compiler treats multiple children as implicitly concurrent, the region structure could be considered present even without explicit separators.
issues.title: CA lacks orthogonal region structure required for concurrent collision avoidance controls

issues.basis: NL2 segment; inspection_equivalent_facts showing reachable_state_count=3 (root, CA, UnspecifiedInitial only) and 9 unreachable states; verify_facts refuting reachability for Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian and all leaf children; FCSTM text showing [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial as CA's only initial edge; LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic confirming UnspecifiedInitial has no outgoing transitions; INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostic on transition:line:32 showing the root entry is conditional
issues.expected: After entry into CA via the root transition, the three operating sub-composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) and their internal states must be reachable so the sub-machine is operationally active and can respond to collision events.
issues.observed: All nine internal states of CA (Frontend, FCIdle, FCActive, RearEnd, RCIdle, RCActive, Pedestrian, PCIdle, PCActive) are unreachable from the root initial entry. CA is itself reachable, but its only internal initial edge ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial, line 30) targets a synthetic dead-end leaf with no outgoing transitions. The verify_facts confirm refuted reachability for all nine states. The LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic on UnspecifiedInitial confirms it is a terminal dead-end.
issues.reason: NL2 requires the sub-machine to become active upon collision detection. Behavioral activation requires reachable internal operating states. The deterministic facts conclusively show all internal states are unreachable because CA's initial entry routes to a dead-end synthetic state rather than the operating composites. This is a root-reachability property distinct from the endpoint existence (satisfied) and the region structure (NL3).
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The unreachable states may become reachable if the trigger on the root-to-CA transition (Possible_collision_detected) fires and the model's concurrent semantics activate all regions simultaneously. However, since CA has no explicit concurrent region structure (no -- separators), standard UML semantics would only activate CA's single initial state, not all child composites.
issues.title: CA operating sub-states unreachable from root initial entry

issues.basis: NL2 segment; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers showing reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for Frontend_collision_detected (consumer transition:line:12), Rear_end_collision_detected (consumer transition:line:19), and Pedestrian_collision_detected (consumer transition:line:26); verify_facts refuting all three event-consumer checks; EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostics for all four internal events; FCSTM text confirming consumer transitions exist only inside the unreachable composite states
issues.expected: The three collision detection events must each have at least one reachable consumer transition within the CA sub-machine scope, so that collision detection can operationally trigger the corresponding avoidance control activation.
issues.observed: All three collision events have declared consumers (Frontend_collision_detected consumed by transition:line:12 in FCIdle, Rear_end_collision_detected by transition:line:19 in RCIdle, Pedestrian_collision_detected by transition:line:26 in PCIdle), but none of these consumer states or transitions are reachable from the root initial entry. The event_consumer facts show reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for all three events. The EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostics confirm this for all four internal events.
issues.reason: NL2 requires the sub-machine to respond to specific collision events. For this response to be operationally possible, the events must have reachable consumers. The deterministic facts show all three collision events are declared and have consumer transitions, but those consumers are in unreachable states. This is an independent event_consumer_coverage property: even if the states were reachable through some other path, the specific consumer coverage question must be assessed. No frozen predicate directly expresses event_consumer_coverage, so this remains a predicate-null candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If the CA region structure defect is fixed (adding concurrent regions), the three sub-composites would become reachable upon CA entry, and their initial states (FCIdle, RCIdle, PCIdle) would be active, making the event consumers reachable. The event consumer coverage issue is therefore a consequence of the upstream region structure and initial entry defects rather than an independent event declaration problem.
issues.title: Collision detection events have no reachable consumer in CA

decisions.reason: The candidate is precisely bound to transition:line:32 (the sole [*] -> CA entry) and the S3 predicate verdict is false: the observed trigger is Possible_collision_detected, not any of the three required events. The grounding is established because the NL2 contract does specify trigger conditions for the entry transition and the exact model facts show a mismatch. However, the NL2 sentence 'This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected' is grammatically ambiguous: the indefinite article 'a' preceding the disjunction could indicate a single detection condition ('a possible [one of three] collision is detected'), in which case Possible_collision_detected faithfully represents that unified condition. The defeater survives because the NL does not explicitly enumerate three separate trigger events or use the UML-precise 'orthogonal' qualifier to disambiguate.

The PlantUML source shows no '--' separators within CA; the canonical IR confirms concurrent_regions count=0; all three child composites reside in a single implicit sequential region.
